contexts.text: They held the Lord as vile.
He esteemed others as viler than himself.
That those in (mere) external worship are most vile; and yet may perform vile services in the Church. Treated of. AC 1097. AC 1103.
They are amended, in order to serve for some vile use.
Man, when born, is the vilest of all living (creatures).

(These) delights are relatively vile; for all delight is such that it is the more vile in proportion as it verges to externals... (Thus) man's delight of pleasures, while he lives in the body, is vile relatively to his delight after (death)... nay, so vile, that good Spirits utterly spurn the delights of the body... and in like manner the delight of these Spirits becomes vile when they are elevated... into the Heaven of angelic Spirits. AC 3938:4.
Grass, etc, = what is vilest (or lowest).
The things of the external man... thus the viler things. Signified.
Those not of the Church, who are more vile. Signified.
A servant of servants = what is lowest in the Church.
He acknowledges... that he is something vile and filthy.
Her mistress was vile in her eyes () = that this Rational, at its conception despised the truth itself adjoined to good. AC 1911:6, Explained AC 1914. AC 1916.
Evil Spirits regard man as a vile slave... Explained. SE 2924.
He begins to hold in slight esteem these delights...
They thus make themselves (unnecessarily) of low estimation...
When (what is good and true, etc.) is regarded as relatively worthless...
They (then) hold as worthless, and loathe, the spiritual things of the internal sense.
A coffer of bulrush = what is of low esteem, but is still derived from truth; thus that truth is of low esteem.
They begin to hold cheap the doctrinals of their faith.
They are not dejected if they are low in station.
Their comparing themselves to dead dogs = that they were to be accounted as utterly worthless...
The delight of life and of Heaven... would gradually become worthless if they were continually in it.
They are sometimes taken out that they may serve others for... low uses.
Servants whom their master holds in slight esteem...
They who have exercised dominion from the love of self... are vile slaves in Hell.
As they either pass by, or hold in slight esteem, the truths of doctrine...
They sink down into a certain prison, where they are called viler than the vile, that is, the vilest.
Emperors and kings... are sometimes less in (the love of rule) than those who are of low origin...
Such a Spirit holds cheap effects or ultimates.
Spiritual things, and confirmatory natural ones, he utterly despised and nauseated as vile and null.
All that honoured her despise her ().
